svg.text: Anatomy of a tool the model can use well — and the same job done badly
Tool(...) as the model sees it (schema) and as the harness runs it (fn, read_only)

g.text: description = "Convert a temperature between Celsius and Fahrenheit.
Returns e.g. '68.0 F'. Use this instead of computing the formula yourself."
or -> "Error: from_unit must be 'C' or 'F' (got 'K'). Example: value=20, from_unit='C'."
← says what it returns and WHEN to use it
← every argument typed, described, with an example
error = what went wrong + what to do instead + a valid example; the model reads it and retries (errors are observations)
read_only lets the permission gate say "allow anything that only reads"; idempotent tools are safe to retry after a timeout
keep results short and shaped (a number, a JSON line, PASS/FAIL + last lines): the model pays for every token twice (read + carry)
could not convert string to float: 'twenty'"
the model must guess what "do" does
what is x? a number? a unit? which way?
a Python traceback tells the model nothing
about the fix; it will retry the same call
an unset flag is a lie to the gate

svg.text: 1. Name = verb_noun. 2. Description says what, when, what comes back. 3. Few arguments, each typed + described + example; no overlapping tools.
4. Errors are text with the fix in them. 5. Declare read_only honestly; make writes idempotent. 6. Bound the output (truncate, paginate, summarise).
7. Sandbox every path and every subprocess. 8. Treat the result as data the model reads, never as instructions (prompt injection, §5).
